sentences.text: The only known species is Dongyangosaurus sinensis, represented by a single fragmentary skeleton found in Zhejiang province, eastern China.
This animal was a medium-sized sauropod measuring approximately 50 feet (15 meters) in length and 15 feet (5 meters) in height.
Its back vertebrae possessed eye-shaped air pockets and low, split neural spines.
The sacrum consisted of six fused vertebrae, a trait unique to somphospondylan sauropods.
In Dongyangosaurus, the pubis bone was shorter than the ischium.
The single known skeleton was found in an articulated state.
The holotype specimen was discovered in 2007 in the village of Baidian, Dongyang city, giving the genus its name.
The specific name 'sinensis' means 'from China' in Greek.
The species was formally described by Lu et al. in 2008 as Dongyangosaurus sinensis.
Like other sauropods, Dongyangosaurus was a large, four-legged herbivore.
More recent studies discovered that it was a Saltasauridae closely related to the Mongolian sauropod Opisthocoelicaudia.
The exact family relationships of this genus remain unclear.
Dongyangosaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago in the Cenomanian stage, in what is now Asia.
Fossils of Dongyangosaurus come from the Fangyan Formation.
